result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers turn down the hero stat and the bigger cards with good reasons, keep all trucks in two dense banks with no scrolling, and save emphasis for exceptions. B is somewhat stronger on alignment and encoding: its column order starts with door, which matches the sort order and explains the visual weight given to each column. It encodes status with a label plus shape or fill instead of color alone, and it gives a filled chip only to the statuses that need action. A is very close and explains well why a hero stat doesn't help, but its column order is less tied to how dispatchers scan, and it relies more on colored chips. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn down the hero stat and the bigger cards, and both keep all trucks visible in two stable, door-sorted banks of dense rows. A is a little stronger on encoding and alignment: it limits filled status chips to the two statuses that need action, keeps the other statuses as plain text, and puts door first so the column order matches the sort order. B gives a clearer reason for dropping the hero stat, but it uses a colored chip for every status and puts the door column after truck ID and carrier even though rows are sorted by door.
